title: Champinjoner till garnityr (Mushrooms as Garnish)
description: Prepared with mushrooms, juice, and water.
steps: The mushrooms are cleaned, as soon as they are picked, in such a way that the scales are removed carefully, the outer skin is not removed from tender mushrooms, the stems are cut off level with the caps, whereupon the mushroom is quickly rinsed and dried on a cloth.
The caps are nicely fluted with a sharp knife, placed immediately in boiling water, seasoned with salt, butter and lemon juice and are allowed to cook 5-10 minutes.
They are taken out with a slotted spoon and used as garnish for finer dishes.
The mushrooms can be stored 2-3 days in a cool place, if they are covered with butter-spread so-called butter paper.
The broth is used for sauces and stews.

description: Prepared with coffee beans, cream, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: sponge fingers or slices of light and dark sponge cake

steps: Roast the coffee, and while it is still warm, pour 2 parts cream over the unground coffee, then let it stand for 0.5 hour in a warm place.

Butter a mold and line it with sponge fingers or with light and dark sponge cake; fill in the cream and set out to stiffen.
Dip it briefly in lukewarm water.
Turn out the pudding and serve.

title: Chateaubrland I (Beef Tenderloin Stuffed with Marrow)
description: Prepared with beef, beef marrow, and shallots.

ingredients.name: 1 tbsp. beef marrow in fine dice for sauce

steps: First cook the sauce: brown the butter, add the onion and brown nicely, add the meat jus, broth and wine, bring to a good boil and strain through a sieve. Let the sauce boil, season with a little paprika, and lastly stir in the parsley and the diced marrow.

Dry the tenderloin with a cloth wrung out in hot water. Carefully remove all outer sinews and membranes, then cut the tenderloin into 6 slices, which are lightly flattened. Make an incision from the side in each slice so that a small opening or pocket is formed. The marrow, which should have soaked in water for 1 hour to draw out the blood, is blanched, i.e. placed in cold salted water and allowed to boil 2-3 minutes without a lid, then drained on a sieve and cooled. Cut into 7 slices (one of which is cut into fine dice and placed in the sauce), brush with melted butter and sprinkle with the chopped onion fried in a little butter. Place the slices into the opening made in the steak, which is pressed shut. Rub the steaks on both sides with the spice mixture and brush with a little butter. Braise or fry in butter 6-8 minutes, taking care that the openings face the pan handle and this is lifted slightly during frying so that the marrow does not flow out. Place on a warm dish, pour the sauce over and serve the dish with small fried potatoes, sprinkled with finely chopped parsley.

description: Prepared with partridges, lard, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: For the sauce: 2 tbsp. butter (40 gr.)

title: Chicken Purée (for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with hen, peppercorns, and stock.
steps: Clean the hen in the usual way and let it soak in plenty of water for 12 hours.
Dry it, cut into 4 pieces, place in cold water with salt added, skim well and let it cook with the spices and 1 liter of the stock until the meat is tender, about 4 hours.
Rinse the rice grains in hot water and let them cook soft in the remaining stock.
When the meat is tender, separate it from the bones, which should boil again in the stock until it makes 2 liters.
Cut the meat into pieces, pass 4 times through a meat grinder and pound in a mortar together with 2 tbsp of the butter and the cooked rice grains.
Pass the forcemeat through a fine sieve.
Strain and skim the stock.
Brown the remaining butter with the flour for 2 minutes, thin the stock little by little, add the forcemeat and let the purée cook while stirring for 5 minutes, then season with the spices.
Whisk the egg yolks in the soup bowl and pour in the purée while whisking vigorously.

title: En smördeg (Butter Dough)
description: Prepared with butter, flour, and water.

ingredients.name: 250 grams fine butter (equal weight to the dough)

steps: Sift the flour and mix it with enough water to make a suitably firm dough, which is worked quickly, weighed, and left to rest for 20 minutes.
Wash the butter and squeeze out the water well, then beat it out into a round cake.

Roll the dough out into a round cake, somewhat thicker in the middle. Place the butter in the centre of the dough and fold the edges of the dough over the butter so that it is completely covered. Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.

Now beat the dough lightly out with a rolling pin into a square of approximately 1/2 cm thickness. This square is then folded together so that the edges of the dough meet in the middle of the square. Then one half of the dough is folded over the other, and the dough lies in four layers on top of each other.
Roll the dough out again into an oblong square. This is repeated 4 times in succession, after which the dough is left to rest for 15 minutes.

Roll it out again 4 times and let it rest for 15 minutes. This is done two more times with the dough, after which it rests for 1 hour before being rolled out into vol-au-vents, bouchées, pastries, butter dough spirals, cakes, etc.
Butter dough is baked in a warm oven.
